nodes.name: Hydrothermal synthesis of Ni(MoO4) precursor
nodes.procedure: Before the experiment, the NF underwent pretreatment. First, NF was ultrasonically cleaned for 10 min each in acetone and in 3 mol L^-1 HCl solution. The predecessor was created using a common hydrothermal method. Specifically, 0.01 M (NH4)6Mo7O24·4H2O and 0.04 M Ni(NO3)2·6H2O were dissolved in 30 mL deionized water under stirring to form a homogeneous solution. In order to produce Ni(MoO4)(H2O)0.7 predecessors, a Teflon-lined stainless-steel autoclave was utilized to house a piece of nickel foam and the aforementioned solution. The autoclave was subsequently sealed and held at 200°C for a duration of 6 h. After completing the reaction, the resulting product was removed, thoroughly cleansed with deionized water to eliminate any residual solution, and left to dry overnight. The resulting precursor was given the name Ni(MoO4)/NF.

nodes.name: Phosphatizing treatment
nodes.procedure: A quartz boat containing a 1 cm×2 cm Ni(MoO4)/NF sample was placed downstream in a tube furnace. Another quartz boat containing 2.0 g sodium hypophosphite was placed upstream in the furnace. The furnace was gradually heated to 500°C at a rate of 5°C min^-1 and kept at that temperature for 120 min under an argon atmosphere. After cooling down to room temperature, the electrode catalyst was obtained and labeled as SA-MoO2/Ni3(PO4)2/NF.

nodes.evidence_snippet: The XRD peaks of SA-MoO₂/Ni₃(PO₄)₂/NF (Figure 2a) at 23.5°, 26.0°, 36.5°, and 40.6° were in accordance with the (102), (111), (113), and (014) lattice plane of Ni₃(PO₄)₂ ... Additional diffraction peaks at 26.0°, 37.0°, 53.5°, and 60.1° are ascribed to the (-111), (-211), (-312), and (031) planes of MoO₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman peaks at 194, 214, 337, 485, 888, 930 cm⁻¹ correspond to Mo=O stretching and lattice deformation of MoO₂; peaks around 200 and 710 cm⁻¹ attributed to phosphate group.
nodes.evidence_snippet: SA-MoO₂/Ni₃(PO₄)₂/NF displays a distinct Raman spectrum featuring prominent peaks at 194, 214, 337, 485, 888, and 930 cm⁻¹ ... It is worth mentioning that the peaks observed around 200 and 710 cm⁻¹ can be attributed to the phosphate group.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows typical microcolumn morphology; lattice-free fringes confirm amorphous surface phase; lattice spacing 0.58 nm corresponds to (110) Ni₃(PO₄)₂ nanoparticle.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The TEM images of SA-MoO₂/Ni₃(PO₄)₂ (Figure 2c) present a typical microcolumn morphology ... Figure 2d shows a layer of lattice-free fringes on the surface of SA-MoO₂/Ni₃(PO₄)₂. The result suggests that an amorphous phase has developed on the surface of the sample.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM confirms amorphous MoOₓ surface layer with lattice spacings 0.343 nm (-111 MoO₂), 0.364 nm (110 Ni₃(PO₄)₂), 0.217 nm (120 Ni₃(PO₄)₂), 0.213 nm (-121 Ni₃(PO₄)₂); SAED and FFT confirm amorphous phases.
nodes.evidence_snippet: An additional HRTEM image shows two distinct sets of lattices spacing, measuring 0.343 and 0.364 nm in width. These measurements correspond to the crystal faces (-111) and (110) of MoO₂ and Ni₃(PO₄)₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS elemental mapping shows Mo, O, Ni, P in bulk; only Mo, O on surface confirming amorphous MoOₓ layer; mass fractions O 24.58%, P 14.23%, Ni 21.66%, Mo 39.52%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The EDS elemental mapping (Figure 2g) exhibits Mo, O, Ni, and P elements on the inner of sample, while only Mo and O are well distributed on the surface of the sample.
The high-resolution XPS spectrum of Ni 2p (Figure 3a) displays two peaks at 856.3 and 874.1 eV, which correspond to the Ni 2p₃/₂ and Ni 2p₁/₂ of Ni²⁺ species in Ni₃(PO₄)₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: EPR signal at g=2.003 confirms oxygen vacancies in the amorphous phase.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The EPR signal of SA-MoO₂/Ni₃(PO₄)₂/NF can be found at a g value of 2.003, indicating a higher level of oxygen vacancies.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES shows bulk composition O 33.18 wt%, P 3.36 wt%, Ni 47.24 wt%, Mo 16.22 wt%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: ICP-OES ... shows percentage weight of 33.18%, 3.36%, 47.24%, and 16.22%, corresponding to O, P, Ni, and Mo element (Table S1, Supporting Information), respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Double layer capacitance Cdl = 220.01 mF cm⁻² indicates large ECSA.
nodes.evidence_snippet: SA-MoO₂/Ni₃(PO₄)₂/NF demonstrates a Cdl value of 220.01 mF cm⁻², outperforming Ni(MoO₄)/NF (0.47) and NF (0.37).

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows microcolumn morphology maintained after phosphating with numerous particles on rough surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: After the phosphating process, the morphology structure was evidently unaltered; although, there were numerous particles on its rough surface (Figure 1d).
